_doc: SURFACE PARITY REGISTRY. This contract exists because zzop shipped the same bug class more than once: the facade computed a field (configWarnings; git-derived health/recommendations/critical; the run-level, join-scoped MultiAnalyzeOutput::warnings channel, e.g. the parallel-implementation tripwire) but the delivery surface silently dropped it. Every top-level field of AnalyzeOutputView and MultiAnalyzeOutputView (crates/facade/src/output.rs) must get exactly one row below, naming what the delivery surface — the MCP analyze_repo/cross_repo reply, which is the SAME shaped summary the `zzop analyze`/`zzop cross` CLI subcommands print (that is the `zzop` binary, packages/cli-bin; `zzop-mcp` takes NO analysis subcommands at all — bare or `mcp` serves stdio and `version`/`help` are the only other forms) — does with it: 'carry' (forwarded unconditionally), 'carry-conditional' (forwarded only in some shaped/capped/gated form, or only when a precondition holds), or 'omit' (never surfaced by the reply). Every 'omit'/'carry-conditional' row MUST carry a non-empty 'note' explaining why and where the data IS available — which, for anything the shaped reply drops, is either the raw zzop-facade output you get by embedding the engine directly or one of the CLI-only lanes in '_cliOnlyLanes' below (since 2026-07-26 `zzop facts` emits the full CommonIr and the whole cross-layer join, so 'available ONLY via a direct embedding' is no longer true of either — check the row's own note). HISTORICAL NOTE: this registry briefly tracked two JS-CLI render surfaces (a pretty terminal render backed by lib/format.js and a markdown report backed by lib/report.js) across the npm distribution's 2026-07-20 removal-then-restoration; @zzop/cli is now a zero-logic shim that spawns the native `zzop` binary with no render logic of its own, so those two columns are dropped again and only the reply lane remains. SCANNED DELIVERY LANE — what an 'omit' row's note means when it says a field is 'never referenced': the meta-test's haystack is every non-test .rs file under THREE directories, crates/summary/src AND packages/mcp/src AND packages/cli-bin/src (canonical list: mcp_lane_dirs() in crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs), minus the `_cliOnlyLanes` implementations declared below. The notes below say 'the scanned delivery lane' and mean all three — never crates/summary/src alone, which would understate the set and let a note read true while packages/mcp/src referenced the field. WHAT AN 'omit' ROW DOES NOT MEAN, and the incident that makes this paragraph load-bearing: 'omit' says THE SHAPED REPLY DOES NOT CARRY THE FIELD, and says nothing whatever about whether anything READS it. The scan behind these notes is narrower than 'does any consumer read this' in two independent ways. (1) MATCHER — it looks for the key literal `"<field>":`, so it sees a re-emission under the field's own name and is structurally blind to a BY-PATH read (`t["output"]["seams"]`, `.get("cache")`, `tree.pointer("/output/ir/loc")`), which is how every consumer of an omitted field in this workspace actually reads it. (2) HAYSTACK — it subtracts every file declared in `_cliOnlyLanes[*].sources`, so a CLI-only lane's consumption is invisible to it BY CONSTRUCTION, and it never scans crates/facade at all, where `query_file`/`query/scan.rs`/`query_coverage` read `ir` by JSON pointer to build the `check_file`/`check_endpoint`/`zzop coverage` answers. On 2026-08-11 a 1.0 readiness reviewer read the four notes that then said an omitted field was reachable 'only via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding)', concluded that nine facade fields (`scores`, `scoreMeanings`, `nodes`, `ir`, `folders`, `seams`, `layerCoChurn`, `coChange`, `cache`) reached no surface at all, and proposed DELETING them before 1.0 froze the contract. Re-measured field by field (`grep -rn '\["<field>"\]\|pointer("[^"]*<field>' --include=*.rs crates packages`), SIX of the nine are read by shipped surfaces and three are not; `ir` alone backs two MCP tools and four CLI lanes, so the deletion would have removed live inputs. A document that guards the code was wrong before the code was. Therefore every 'omit' row below now states EITHER its by-path consumers with file and line, OR that a by-path search was run and found none — and 'none' means the search ran, not that a field-name grep came back empty. WHAT GUARDS THIS PROSE, AND WHAT STILL DOES NOT — read this before writing a note. crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs checks the `mcpAnalyzeReply` markers against the real lane, checks that every field of the view has a row, and checks that an 'omit'/'carry-conditional' row's `note` is NON-EMPTY. Since 2026-08-11 it also checks the SHAPE of every 'omit' row's note: the note must contain either a cited consumer written `<file>.rs:<line>` or the literal `grep -rn`, recording that a by-path search was RUN. That is the direct fix for the incident above — the reviewer acted on a sentence that asserted 'nothing reads this' with no evidence attached, and such a sentence now fails the build. It is NOT a truth check and cannot be one: a note that cites a real file:line but describes it wrongly stays green, and so does a note that invents a plausible-looking citation. What the guard converts is UNFALSIFIABLE prose into a claim the next reader can check in one command. Deliberately scoped to 'omit' rows only: a 'carry-conditional' note says the field DOES reach the surface under a stated condition, so it makes no no-consumer claim and has no consumer to cite — demanding one there would produce decorative citations. Nine rows carry the check today. ONE COLUMN, TWO REPLIES — read this before writing a status. `mcpAnalyzeReply` names one delivery LANE that ships two documents, and which one a row speaks about is decided by its ROOT, not by the column: an `analyzeOutputView` row answers for the `analyze_repo`/`zzop analyze` reply, a `multiAnalyzeOutputView` row for the `cross_repo`/`zzop cross` reply. The consequence is a real blind spot and it has been paid for: a PER-TREE field also has a fate inside the cross reply (dropped, carried in a `sources[]` row, or lifted to the join root), and no column states it — while TEST 3's key-literal haystack is the WHOLE lane (crates/summary/src includes cross.rs), so a `carry` satisfied by the join projection reads as though the analyze reply forwarded it. Measured 2026-08-29: `nativeAnalyses` sat at `carry-conditional` on its own row and was absent from every byte of the cross reply, root and `sources[]` alike, with nothing red. Do not fix this by adding a second status column: `registry_surfaces` derives the surface set from the rows and then demands every column on EVERY row, so a cross column would force a nonsense status onto the five `multiAnalyzeOutputView` rows, whose reply the first column already describes. The two mechanisms that DO cover it are `_replyRootKeys` below (top-level keys, machine-checked against a real reply) and behavioural pins in crates/summary/tests; what remains uncovered is the inside of a `sources[]` element, and multiAnalyzeOutputView.trees's note says so. REPLY-ROOT KEYS: a reply key that is not a field of either view can hold no row here (TEST 1/2 pin each root's key set to a facade view) — declare it in `_replyRootKeys` instead, in the same commit, or crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs goes red naming it. A NOTE MAY NOT CONTRADICT ITS OWN COLUMN. If a note spells ``X`, not `Y`` or ``X` rather than `Y`` where both are status tokens, X must BE this row's status; surface_parity.rs enforces it. The rule reads pedantic and was written from an incident: the `nativeAnalyses` and `nativeAnalysesMeaning` rows landed declaring `carry-conditional`, each opening with a paragraph explaining why `carry` is not honest here, and each asserting `carry` further down in the SAME note — a status edit applied to the column and to the first paragraph but not to the last. Nothing was red, because every check on a note was about its emptiness or its citations, never about whether it agreed with the row it sits in. State a status once, in the column, and let the prose explain it. WORKFLOW FOR FUTURE BATCH AGENTS: adding a field to AnalyzeOutputView or MultiAnalyzeOutputView? Add this registry's row for it IN THE SAME COMMIT — crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs's completeness test fails the build otherwise, by design. This file documents TODAY's truth, not an aspiration: a row reflects what the code actually does, not what it should eventually do.

_cliOnlyLanes._doc: Delivery lanes that exist ONLY on the `zzop` CLI, with the reason each has no MCP tool twin, and the .rs files that implement each one's PROJECTION. What `sources` means, precisely, because the subtraction below depends on it: the projection implementation under crates/summary/** — NOT the argv entry points that route to it (packages/cli-bin/src/main.rs and its cli/ module). Those files are deliberately NOT declared, and must not be: they also dispatch lanes that are NOT CLI-only (`analyze`, `cross`, `endpoint`), so subtracting them wholesale would blind the haystack to a real MCP-lane leak in exactly the files where argv meets the shared handlers. The consequence of leaving them in is FAIL-SAFE, which is why it is the right side to err on: if an argv file ever emits an `omit` field's key literal, the guard reads it as an MCP-lane leak and goes RED (a false red someone must then explain), never green. As of 2026-07-26 neither file spells any registry field name as a JSON key literal outside a comment, so nothing is failing today. The PROSE here is documentation (the meta-test's SURFACES list in crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/surface_parity.rs covers `mcpAnalyzeReply` alone) — recorded so a future batch does not 'restore parity' by adding a twin without re-reading why there isn't one. The `sources` arrays, however, ARE machine-read (since 2026-07-26): that meta-test's carry/omit check subtracts exactly those files from the MCP lane it scans, so this block is what defines the boundary between 'a CLI-only lane deliberately emits this' and 'the MCP reply leaks it'. Consequences, both deliberate: a lane that ships without declaring its sources leaves them inside the MCP lane and fails the build the moment it emits an `omit` field (declare the lane, do not rename the key around the guard); and a declared path that no longer resolves is a hard failure, so a moved lane source must update this file in the same commit. The subtraction applies to `carry` rows too — a CLI-only emission must never be what keeps a `carry` row green after the MCP reply stopped forwarding it. NOTE for the `zzop manifest` and `zzop facts` rows below: because both read fields the shaped reply drops, an `omit` row's note can no longer say 'available ONLY via a direct zzop-facade embedding' without qualification — see the `ir` row. Since 2026-08-15 the sources arrays are machine-read in the OTHER direction too (every_non_test_rs_inside_a_declared_lane_module_tree_is_itself_declared, same test file): every non-test .rs inside a declared lane's module tree must itself be declared; a tree's ENTRY file (its mod.rs, or the <name>.rs beside the directory) must stay declared, or its still-declared siblings fail the build naming it; and the honest fix for a genuinely-shared file depends on where the lane lives — under a TEST 3 haystack directory it must MOVE OUT of the lane tree (a declaration would widen the subtraction unverified), while outside the haystack (the zzop explain lane, crates/facade) a declaration subtracts nothing, so classify honestly and declare. A LANE CAN LEAVE THIS OBJECT, and one has: `zzop coverage` sat here until 2026-09-04 with a `noMcpTwinBecause` that ENDED "if agent demand for the AGGREGATE arrives, promote then — the twin is a dispatch entry away". The demand it was waiting for was already the reason the surface exists (an agent reading a zero needs to know whether the tool could see anything at all), so the sentence had become a deferral wearing a judgment's clothes, and `check_coverage` shipped. Its projection file (crates/summary/src/coverage.rs) therefore RE-ENTERED TEST 3's haystack in the same commit, which is why the row was removed rather than reworded: a lane declared here is SUBTRACTED from the leak scan, so leaving a now-MCP-reachable file declared would have made this guard quieter about the exact file that had just gained a wire.

zzop manifest.emits: Identity rows only — provides {kind,key,source}, edges {kind,key,from,to}, buckets {bucket,kind,key,source} — sorted, deduped, UNCAPPED, plus a `tool` fingerprint (zzop_facade::version_string) and per-source {joinContributionZero, degraded}. No file, no line, no root path, no findings.
zzop manifest.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) The manifest is deliberately UNCAPPED, and every MCP reply this repo ships is cap-governed (the token-bomb guard crates/summary/src/output exists for); putting it on that wire would force a choice between breaking that doctrine and capping the one artifact whose whole reason for existing is that the caps make two capped summaries un-diffable above them. (2) The workflow is file-shaped, not conversation-shaped: a manifest earns its keep by being COMMITTED and compared by a later run (the scripts/max-file-lines-baseline.txt model). (3) An agent that wants it can shell out to the same binary — the analysis path is identical.

reads: two `zzop manifest` outputs — no engine, no filesystem beyond the two files
zzop diff.emits: transitions (a key's bucket placement changed — the ranked signal), sources {added, removed, coverageDropped}, and per-relation added/removed for provides/edges/buckets, with `blindnessSuspect` on any removal attributable to a source that lost coverage.
zzop diff.noMcpTwinBecause: It consumes manifests; without a `manifest` twin an agent could not produce its own inputs, so a diff-only tool would be half a surface. Ships with `manifest` or not at all.

reads: trees[].output.gitWindow (presence only — the gate on whether git collection ran)
trees[].output.nodes[].{path,changeCount,churn,authorCount,lastModified} (the dep domain's history axes, read only when that gate says git ran)
trees[].output.scores (presence only — the numbers are deliberately NOT drawn)
zzop graph.emits: TWO FORMATS, selected by `--format`, because its consumer is a renderer rather than a parser. (A) `--format mermaid` (DEFAULT, every domain) — MERMAID TEXT, the one zzop product that is not a JSON document. (B) `--format cosmograph-nodes|cosmograph-links` (`--domain dep` ONLY, a usage error elsewhere) — NDJSON tables for an interactive viewer, one record per line, emitted UNCAPPED: `--top` is refused rather than ignored, because capping exists to keep a DRAWN picture readable and a viewer with zoom does that job itself. Measured on zzop's own tree, mermaid draws 40 of 1165 files where this lane emits all 1165 and all 2154 edges (re-measured 2026-08-01; the figure moves with the repo, so it is illustrative of the RATIO, not a pinned constant), which is the case dep.rs's module doc reserved when it said a large graph is where a different format stays live. Both formats read the SAME uncapped `dep::collect` pass, so they cannot become two answers about one repo. The nodes table carries the axes a viewer styles by; the links table carries `source`/`target`/`endpointsInCycle` — named for the ENDPOINT test it actually runs (both ends are members of some reported cycle), because the reported cycles are flattened into one member set, so a chord inside a cycle and an edge bridging two DIFFERENT cycles both score true without lying on a cycle themselves; the NODE column keeps the name `inCycle`, where claim and computation agree. Nine node columns are STRUCTURAL — `id`/`source`/`path`/`label`/`folder`/`fanIn`/`fanOut`/`degree`/`inCycle`, where `label` is a basename — derived from the graph itself, so every row has them. The rest are MEASURED and ride only when this run measured them: `loc` (from `ir.loc`) and, when `gitWindow` says git collection ran, `changeCount`/`churn`/`authorCount`/`lastModified` (from `nodes[]`). No flag adds or removes a column — a schema that changed per invocation is one no consumer could write against — so what varies is whether a ROW HAS a key. An unmeasured axis is OMITTED, never written as `0`: `churn: 0` would say 'never changed' in the same bytes as 'nobody looked', and a viewer colouring by it would draw the second as the first. That is also why the git axes are gated on `gitWindow` rather than read field-by-field: `nodes[]` is built unconditionally and its counters default to `0`, so on a git-off run every row on the wire carries a perfectly-formed `changeCount: 0`. NDJSON rather than CSV so `serde_json` owns quoting (a path containing a comma cannot silently shift columns). DISCLOSURE GOES TO STDERR for this format, never into the table: stdout is a parseable table and a `%%` census line would be a corrupt row, so the CLI prints the scope/total census on the other stream — and that census also reports how many emitted rows carried each MEASURED axis (`loc on N of M row(s), git history on N of M`), because omitting an unmeasured column is honest but silent: without the count, a reader whose viewer offers no colour-by-churn has nothing to read. A `flowchart LR` with one subgraph per analyzed source and one node per (sourceId, side, kind, key): rectangles for provides, stadiums for consumes, solid arrows for resolved edges, DOTTED arrows for the two non-authoritative relations (an ambiguous consume to each candidate provider, and an edge the linker flagged `lowConfidenceReason`). Each node's bucket rides its LABEL as well as its `classDef` class, so a viewer that drops styling still reads the verdict. SCOPED BY CONSTRUCTION: `--top` caps DRAWN RELATIONS per bucket (default 25, no upper bound — a file/pipe surface, not the capped wire; rows are deduped to distinct relations BEFORE the cap, because a node aggregates call sites and a row-based cap described a picture the reader was not looking at — measured on the OSS corpus, 60 `edges` rows are 4 relations) and `--scope <prefix>` keeps rows whose source id or a site path starts with the prefix; both are disclosed twice, in a `%%` per-bucket drawn/inScope/total-relations census that also publishes the call-site count each aggregates, AND as a visible note node, since a mermaid comment does not survive rendering. NOT emitted, and named in the document's own header rather than left to inference: `crossLayerFindings` (the drift/near-miss VERDICTS — findings ABOUT the join, not members of it; a finding has no node identity here and inventing one would be inventing facts the IR does not have), `hostRekeyCounts` (a counter, not an edge), the warnings/configWarnings/disclosure prose channels, and per-site file/line (nodes AGGREGATE call sites — `zzop facts`/`zzop cross`'s `distinctBucketKeyFirstSites` carry sites). An item with neither `key` nor `raw` is counted as an unlabelable remainder in the census, never guessed at.
zzop graph.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) A diagram is a terminal/file act — `zzop graph ./api ./web > join.mmd` then a renderer — the same file- and pipe-shaped lane `manifest` and `facts` argued for. ⚠ CORRECTED 2026-09-13 (ledger V226): this reason used to end "an agent that wants the picture shells out to the same binary for identical bytes", and that half is FALSE for the audience it was written about — an MCP client has no shell and cannot invoke a binary. It is the same mistake ledger V219 found in an error message, made here about a whole lane. What survives is the first half: the OUTPUT is file- and pipe-shaped. The decision stands on reasons (2) and (3) and on that half, not on a shell an agent does not have. (2) The shaped answers already exist on the MCP wire: `cross_repo` carries the same buckets as counts, keys and sites, which is what a PROGRAM reasons over, while a flowchart is for a human eye. A tool twin would put the same data on two surfaces under two different shaping rules — the exact drift class this registry exists to prevent. (3) Since the cosmograph format landed, this lane also emits an UNCAPPED table — 1165 nodes and 2154 edges on zzop's own tree — which is the same argument `manifest` and `facts` make, only now it applies to a lane whose reader is explicitly a HUMAN at a viewer rather than an agent in a conversation. Putting it on the cap-governed wire would force capping the one output whose reason for existing is that it is not capped.

zzop facts.emits: The whole post-assembly FACT SUBSTRATE, UNCAPPED and verbatim: `{tool, config, configWarnings, trees[{sourceId, coverage, warnings, commonIr}], crossLayer, warnings, disclosure}`. The consumer half of the custom-rule extension point — zzop emits what it knows and a user's own program decides what is a problem. It executes nothing (no process spawn) and ingests nothing (no findings channel back in). NOT emitted: zzop's own `findings`/`crossLayerFindings` (verdicts, not facts — a rule author computes their own, and carrying ours would put the same data on two surfaces under two different caps), and `AttributeStore` (the one post-assembly fact whose CONTAINER is not already a serialized wire shape; emitting it would freeze a NEW shape, which this repo's projection-contract bar gates behind a consuming rule existing first). KEY NAMING: the per-tree IR rides under `commonIr`, not `ir` — a design choice, and (since 2026-07-26) no longer a guard workaround: the meta-test enforcing the `ir` row's `omit` status now subtracts this lane's `sources`, so either spelling would pass it. `commonIr` camel-cases the exact type a rule author has to look up to read the block (`zzop_core::CommonIr`, field list in docs/modules/facade.md) and stays greppable inside a consumer's own codebase, which a two-letter key that is a substring of `circular`/`directory`/`require` is not. The cost is one mapping to remember, because a direct zzop-facade embedding spells the same block `ir` — stated in the `ir` row below so a reader diffing the two surfaces meets it there.
zzop facts.noMcpTwinBecause: (1) The output is deliberately UNCAPPED and grows with tree size, while every MCP reply this repo ships is cap-governed (crates/summary/src/output) — the same argument the `ir` row already makes for the analyze reply, only stronger: `ir` alone measured 107x the shipped reply on zzop's own tree and `facts` carries the whole join on top. The main MCP consumer is an AI agent, so output size is a direct context cost. (2) The consumer is a PROGRAM, not a conversation: the workflow is `zzop facts ./api ./web > facts.json && ./my-rule facts.json`, a terminal/CI act. (3) An agent already has the shaped answers it usually wants (join buckets, check_endpoint); `facts` exists for the case those cannot serve, which is precisely the case that is not a conversation. An agent that genuinely wants it can shell out to the same binary for the identical answer.

reads: nothing from a run — the bundled DSL pack data compiled INTO the binary
zzop explain.emits: One rule's compiled-in data as human-readable lines, or a guided Err naming what the id actually is (a native analysis id, a pack id, an output field id, an ambiguous bare id, or unknown).
zzop explain.noMcpTwinBecause: It answers from data that is already ON the MCP wire — and since 2026-09-13 (`7854d1ad`) that is PER ID, not only as a whole: the `zzop://rule/{id}` resource template serves one DSL rule's full text, the same bytes this subcommand prints. The `rule-catalog` resource remains the whole-catalog form and is the only route for a NATIVE analysis id, which `zzop://rule/{id}` refuses. So there is no tool twin because the answer is a RESOURCE rather than a tool call, not because an agent must read the catalog. 🔴 This field carried the older reasoning — "an agent looks a rule up by reading one document rather than by calling a tool per id" — for a day past the commit that inverted it, and `docs/rules/catalog.md` cited THIS field to tell MCP clients that exact matcher values were unreachable to them while the resource was serving those values. Found by external review round 22 (2026-09-14, ledger V244). The subcommand still exists because a TERMINAL user wants one rule, not the catalog. Declared here — even though its projection lives in crates/facade rather than crates/summary — because the one-audience fact is what both consumers of this block need: crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/host_vocabulary.rs's contract 16 subtracts these files when it checks that shared crates name no CLI-only vocabulary, and naming `zzop explain` inside the `zzop explain` lane is correct, not a leak. NOT declared, deliberately: `zzop init`. Its only implementation is the argv entry point (packages/cli-bin/src/cli/run.rs), which this block's `_doc` forbids declaring, and the bytes it writes are a two-audience contract resource that MCP `resources/read` serves as well.

_laneTwins._doc: LANE TWINS — the CLI subcommand and the MCP tool that are the SAME lane, declared because their names do not derive from one another. WHY THIS BLOCK EXISTS (2026-09-15): contracts 15/16 in crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/host_vocabulary.rs let a shared-crate message name a host spelling when it names that spelling's TWIN in the same breath — and it resolved the twin MECHANICALLY, by swapping `-` for `_`. That works for three lanes (analyze-envelope, validate-envelope, validate-rule-pack) and is false for the other six, where the tool is named for the QUESTION (`check_coverage`) and the subcommand for the OBJECT (`coverage`). Nothing was red, because no shared message had ever named both halves of such a pair: the derivation's blind spot was invisible while its population was empty. It stopped being empty when the sightline census in crates/engine/src/disclosure/registry/analysis.rs was corrected to name both hosts — until then it told MCP readers the visibility lane was CLI-only, which had been false since `check_coverage` shipped on 2026-09-04, and an EXEMPTION was what kept it green (an exemption records why a spelling is honest; no guard re-asks whether the reason still holds). CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS by host_vocabulary.rs: each pair's CLI half must be a subcommand main.rs really dispatches and its MCP half a tool packages/mcp/src/tools/definitions.rs really ships, and EVERY shipped tool must appear here — so a new tool either declares its twin or fails the build naming itself. A tool that genuinely has no CLI twin is a new kind of row and needs a decision, not a silent omission; `_cliOnlyLanes` above is the mirror for the other direction.

buildScriptPaths.note: The tree's own package.json `scripts` path tokens, resolved against the walked file set and sorted (zzop_engine::AnalyzeOutput::build_script_paths). Omitted from the reply but NOT unconsumed — it is the third input to the shaped reply's finding ORDER: `crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs:67` reads it by key and `crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs:73` hands it to `output::shape_findings`, whose deployment-role tier sorts findings on these files after every production and test-path finding, ahead of severity rather than within one band (`crates/summary/src/output/deployment_role.rs` is the judgment). Measured, not assumed: `grep -rn 'buildScriptPaths' --include=*.rs crates packages` returns the producer field (`crates/facade/src/output.rs:71`), the facade's own key-set and value pins (`crates/facade/src/analyze_tests.rs`), exactly ONE runtime read (`crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs:67`), and doc-comment mentions in the shaper — no other surface, no CLI-only lane, no query core. The by-path search matters here for the reason `_doc` gives: a key read via `output_view["buildScriptPaths"]` is a bracket index, not a struct field, so a field-name scan alone would have called this row unconsumed. What a reader sees of it is therefore the `findings.buildPaths` disclosure, which carries the COUNT and the sentence; the path list itself would be a second, larger copy of a fact the ordering already applied. Available whole via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding). ALWAYS serialized at the facade boundary, `[]` included: every tree outside the npm ecosystem declares no build script by construction, and an empty array is what separates 'walked, declared nothing' from 'an engine build that does not report this'.

cache.note: Cache PROVENANCE. Was `omit` until 2026-08-17 on the reading that hit/miss counts are an internal performance diagnostic; the counts are also the only thing in the reply that separates a RECOMPUTED finding list from one REPLAYED off disk, which made a manufactured zero (a hand-edited cache entry, measured with the credential still in the source) unanswerable from the reply alone. The shaper now forwards a projection — {hitFiles, missFiles, fileCount, meaning} via `output::cache_signal` — not the raw `CacheStatsView`, and only when a cache was in play, so a run with caching off grows no key (absent, never null, same contract as architecture/ruleTimings). `--profile-rules` still reads `output.cache.hits` by JSON path for its own disclosure; the two derive from one field rather than one of them re-deriving it.

coChange.note: Never forwarded on the shaped reply, but NOT unconsumed: the shipped CLI lane `zzop graph --domain cochange` reads `output.coChange` BY JSON PATH (`crates/summary/src/graph/cochange.rs:80`), which no field-name scan shows — that file is a declared `_cliOnlyLanes` source (subtracted from the haystack) and the read is a path index rather than a key literal, so the scan is blind to it twice over (see `_doc`). The omission is for the same reason `ir` is omitted and NOT because it is bulky: the edge list is UNBOUNDED in tree size (one entry per surviving file pair — 972 on zzop's own tree, `zzop graph --domain cochange --top 100000 | grep -c ' --- '`), while the shipped reply is capped. AVAILABILITY: the CLI-only `zzop graph --domain cochange` lane draws it, capped by `--top` and with that cap plus the two upstream filters disclosed inside the document itself; a direct zzop-facade embedding yields the whole array. NOT interchangeable with `layerCoChurn`: that field keeps only pairs CROSSING an architectural layer, so it cannot answer 'what changes together' inside one module, which is this field's whole subject. A consumer must also keep `null` and `[]` apart — `null` means git was inactive (nothing measured), `[]` means it was measured and no pair survived.

critical.note: Only the top 3 paths (the engine's own SIZE-WEIGHTED blast-radius ranking: blast_radius * ln(loc+2), with blast radius as the tie-break — crates/metrics/src/criticality.rs::compute_criticality) ride the compact `architecture.criticalTop` summary (crates/summary/src/analyze/architecture.rs::architecture_summary). findings.note: Shaped via output::shape_findings into {total, bySeverity, byRule, byRuleMeaning, shown (the window order of crates/summary/src/output/ordering.rs — deployment role desc, then severity desc, then three keys that interleave rather than rank: distinct file:line, then distinct (rule, file), then rule round-robin, with the engine's own (severity, file, line, ruleId) as the deterministic tiebreak; capped at DEFAULT_FINDINGS_LIMIT=50 unless the caller supplies `limit`), shownMeaning (the legend that says that sequence is an ORDER and not a RANKING, and that no per-finding confidence backs it — folded to a note plus a pointer, full text in the reply-legends contract document), truncated?, testPaths?, buildPaths?, note?, ruleMessages?, ruleMessagesMeaning?, ruleMessageTemplates?, ruleMessageTemplatesMeaning?, messageByIdMeaning?} — never the raw findings array verbatim. Each entry of `shown` carries `message` as a string always; a text that MORE THAN ONE shown finding carries AND whose folding removes more bytes than the pointer, the `messageRef` field and the table cost to add is stored once in a sibling `ruleMessages` object (`{key: text}`, keyed by rule id, `<ruleId>#2` for a rule's later distinct texts) and those findings carry `messageRef` holding the key plus a short pointer `message`. The gate is net bytes, not repetition, and it is applied per text: a short message repeated inside one reply stays inline while a long one beside it folds, because the pointer plus the field plus the row cost about 260 bytes a finding and 45 of the 118 shipped messages are cheaper carried twice than folded once. A SECOND table folds what that key cannot reach: a rule that writes a finding's own subject into its prose (a table name, a symbol, a cycle path) emits a different string every time, so its shared segments are stored in a sibling `ruleMessageTemplates` (`{ruleId: [segment, ...]}`, keyed by the rule id with no `#N`) and each such finding carries `templateParts`, the bytes that differ, in order. Rebuild by interleaving segment-first and ending on the last segment; `templateParts` is always exactly one shorter than the template, a segment may be empty at either end, one template serves a rule, and no finding ever carries both `templateParts` and `messageRef`. Same net-byte gate and same losslessness — measured on the `analyze` lane against cal.com at `--limit 1000`, 1,705,102 to 993,947 bytes (-41.7%) with all 1,000 messages rebuilding byte-identically, and at `--limit 50` byte-identical to the reply before it, because a fifty-row window holds no template worth its pointer. Both `ruleMessages` and its legend `ruleMessagesMeaning` are additive-only — absent, never empty — so a reply whose every message is unique is byte-identical to what it was before the fold existed. The fold runs on `shown` AFTER the cap, is lossless (`crates/summary/src/output/rule_prose/`), and moves no count: resolve with `ruleMessages[finding.messageRef]` or `ruleMessageTemplates[finding.ruleId]`, never by parsing the pointer sentence, which `VERSIONING.md` keeps explicitly outside the compatibility surface while freezing the field names. A THIRD mechanism removes prose from the reply rather than deduplicating it, and it is the only one of the three that is not resolvable from this reply alone. A finding carrying `messageBy` holds a pointer in `message`: its rule declared that text word for word, so the reader rebuilds it from the finding's own `ruleId` through `zzop explain <ruleId>` on the CLI or the `zzop://rule/{id}` resource template on MCP, which serve the same bytes from the same function (that function also prints the disable knob, which used to ride only on the finding). DETECT IT BY THE FIELD, never by the sentence: `messageBy` names the resolver (`ruleId` is the only value today) and is the contract, while the sentence is wording and this document's own exclusion list frees wording to change. No finding ever carries more than one of `messageBy`, `messageRef` and `templateParts`. `messageByIdMeaning` discloses the lane: an additive-only sibling legend present exactly when some shown finding carries the field and absent otherwise, so a reply with none is byte-identical to one from before this existed. Four classes are never pointed away and keep every byte inline — a native analysis (no declared message exists to restore from); a near-miss rewrite (the matcher spliced a marker token it found in the reader's own SOURCE into the prose, and that token is in no other field of the finding); a rule this binary does not carry, because both resolvers answer only for rules compiled in, so a pack loaded from `zzop/rules/` or `packs.extraDirs` keeps its prose rather than being pointed at a door that would answer `unknown rule id`; and any rule whose whole assembled message is cheaper than the pointer and its field, the same net-byte gate `ruleMessages` applies. The pointer is written by the SHAPER (`crates/summary/src/output/rule_prose/by_id.rs`), which is why the three entry points this table freezes as one row agree by construction, and why `zzop_facade::analyze_trees_json` — a data producer with nine consumers in that crate — hands every one of them the full prose. No finding is removed and no count moves — `total`, `bySeverity` and `byRule` never read `message` — and `truncated` below remains the only key that means rows were left out. Measured through the CLI on `cases/trees/api-be` at the default window (`zzop analyze cases/trees/api-be | wc -c`): 127,937 bytes before this lane existed, 61,531 after, -51.9%. 46 of the 50 shown findings carry the field; the 4 that keep their prose are native. The MCP lane measures a different envelope (JSON-RPC framing), so a number quoted here is the CLI one. `truncated` is {shown, totalMatching, severitiesNotShown, hint}: `severitiesNotShown` ({counts, firstOmitted, meaning}, always present inside `truncated`) names the severity bands the cut removed OUTRIGHT, counted over the post-filter set the cap was applied to, because role-first ordering can push a whole `critical` band past the cap while `bySeverity` keeps counting it (cal.com at --limit 1000: `critical: 6` beside 1000 rows carrying none). `firstOmitted` carries, per silenced severity, that band's first cut rows as `ruleId`/`file`/`line` in the same order `shown` uses — a bounded SAMPLE (at most 3 a severity; `counts` stays exact) and no `message`, so a run whose exit code turned on a band nothing in `shown` carries still names sites the reader can open. `zzop analyze --fail-on` reads those sites back onto stderr when the reply's own list holds none of the rows it gated on; the gate itself still decides on `bySeverity` alone, so no view knob has entered the verdict. The `hint` drops "raise the limit" at limit == MAX_LIMIT, where a larger value is a usage error rather than a remedy. `note` is the zero-match disclosure for the `rule` and `severity` filters, present only when a filter was given and matched nothing (both notes join into the one key when both fired): an empty `shown` from a real-but-quiet rule and an empty `shown` from a TYPO are the same bytes without it. The two path keys are ordering DISCLOSURES, not filters: shipped code sorts before test paths, which sort before build surface, ahead of severity rather than within one tier (crates/summary/src/output/deployment_role.rs), and each demoted tier publishes its own full-set count. Both are additive-only — absent, never `{count: 0}` — so a tree with no test or build surface pays no bytes for the axis.

nativeAnalyses.note: STATUS NOTE: `carry-conditional` rather than `carry`, and the reason is about the GUARD, not about the field — it is forwarded under its own name on every reply this build produces. `carry` is asserted by one mechanism only, `surface_parity.rs`'s grep for the literal `"<field>":`, which that test's own doc says a key inserted by name (`summary.insert("nativeAnalyses".to_string(), ..)`) is invisible to in both directions; the shipped `carry` rows satisfy it incidentally, from cross.rs's `json!` rows. Contorting the shaper to plant a substring would make the code worse and prove nothing extra. `carry-conditional` is also literally accurate: the forward is `.get()`-gated so an older engine/facade degrades to omission rather than a JSON `null`, exactly `packsLoadedMeaning`'s lane. It is listed in crates/summary/src/analyze/tests.rs's CONDITIONAL_UNDER_ITS_OWN_NAME, and the enforcement it trades up to is BEHAVIORAL rather than textual: `the_shaped_reply_carries_the_native_analyses_disclosure_and_its_legend` runs the shaper and asserts both keys with their content. NOW THE FIELD ITSELF: the native counterpart of `packsLoaded`: {registered, disabled, shippedOff, reportedInCrossLayerFindings} — how many native analyses this build registers and which of them could not have keyed this reply's findings map, split by CAUSE. Added 2026-08-28 after a whole-catalog audit found 106 of 184 catalogued ids absent from every reply and no channel able to say why; the DSL half of that question was already answered by packsLoaded's `didNotRun`/`zeroAdmissionRules`, and the native half had no channel at all. UNCONDITIONAL IN SUBSTANCE — which is a different question from the STATUS above, and conflating the two is what left this row contradicting itself for a day (it declared `carry-conditional`, opened with the STATUS NOTE explaining why, and then asserted `carry` twice further down; a half-finished edit, and no guard held the prose against its own column). The FIELD is unconditional: the object is a statement about the BUILD rather than about the caller's request, so unlike ruleOverridesApplied there is no 'nothing was asked' state, and every inner list serializes even when empty — the deliberate break with `zeroAdmissionRules`'s skip-if-empty convention, because a channel whose population is 'what I found' reports nothing on a clean run in bytes indistinguishable from one that never ran. Every list is DERIVED per run from the registrations themselves (`zzop_engine::register_all_native` for the population, `zzop_rules_cross_layer::register_native_analyses` for the cross-layer subset, `zzop_engine::shipped_off_native_ids` for the shipped-off one) and gated through `zzop_core::is_enabled`, the same call the evaluator makes, so no count here can drift from the registry or from the gate; the floor that stops a broken derivation reading as 'everything was evaluated' is crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/native_analyses.rs. THE THIRD CAUSE, added 2026-09-03: `shippedOff` names registered analyses THIS BUILD ships switched off which the config did not turn on — `unimported-export`, `dead-candidates`, `unreachable`, 61.7% of every finding across the dogfood corpus and all three `info`. It is a separate list rather than a fold into `disabled` because `disabled` is read as "the caller chose this", and a project default listed there tells every reader they made a decision they did not make; the two are disjoint by construction, being one `is_enabled` answer partitioned on whether the id is in the caller's own `disabled_rules`. The join reply has no such key, and giving it one would require inventing a fact: the join gate is EXCLUDE-ONLY, so whether a shipped-off analysis ran is settled per TREE, and a config that opted in for one tree and not another has no honest single entry (a union calls it skipped where it ran; an intersection calls it run where it was skipped). The join legend's `everythingElse` sentence names that case and points at the per-tree roster instead. The join's cross-layer POPULATION is separately safe: each tree's `reportedInCrossLayerFindings` is already `is_enabled`-filtered, so a shipped-off cross-layer id could not reach the union the join builds — a property of the current set rather than of the design, asserted in crates/engine/tests/rule_contracts/native_analyses.rs. THE JOIN LANE, added 2026-08-29: the same roster now also rides the `cross_repo`/`zzop cross` reply at its ROOT, derived for the run the join actually gated (crates/summary/src/cross/native_analyses.rs) and declared in `_replyRootKeys.cross_repo` below, because a per-tree field lifted to the join root is not a `multiAnalyzeOutputView` field and so can hold no row of its own. It carries an EXTRA key there, `zeroInCrossLayerFindings` — the population minus the keys of `crossLayerFindings.byRule` — which only that reply can compute, and its legend forks: in a per-tree reply `reportedInCrossLayerFindings` means `run the join`, while in the join reply those analyses ARE the channel being read. Measured before the fix: the cross reply carried the roster nowhere (not at the root, not on any of nine `sources[]` rows) while its own byRule held 18 keys against a 27-analysis roster. Pinned behaviourally by crates/summary/tests/cross_native_analyses.rs, including a two-directional canary (one tree disables one id; it must leave the population and appear under `disabled`). Forwarded to the MCP/CLI shaped reply by crates/summary/src/analyze/shape.rs, which is the lane the defect was measured on: `zzop analyze` over each of nine single-tree corpus configs reported zero `cross-layer/*` keys while the cross-layer join over the SAME nine configs produced 975 findings on 9 trees of 9.

nativeAnalysesMeaning.note: Same status and same reason as its sibling row above — see that note for why `carry` is not the honest label for a key the shaper inserts by name. The legend for `nativeAnalyses`: build-constant sentences keyed `registered`, `disabled`, `shippedOff`, `reportedInCrossLayerFindings` and `everythingElse` (the residual class with no field of its own, precisely because it is the case where absence IS the verdict). `shippedOff` joined on 2026-09-03 and the residual sentence had to move with it — it read "a registered analysis in NEITHER list ran", which a third list makes false in the dangerous direction, so it now says NONE of the three. The same count sits in the folded `nativeAnalysesMeaning` note (`zzop_summary`'s "Four ways it is not"), which is the copy that ships on the reply. The residual sentence used to say that absence from `findings` is a measured zero FULL STOP, which its own neighbour `registered` contradicted for two registration classes — score-gating ids that emit no finding at all, and umbrella ids whose findings arrive under finer `schema/<label>` ids; it now carves those out by name and defers to `registered` for their description, pinned by a position test in crates/facade/src/output/native_analyses_legend.rs. The JOIN reply carries its own sibling of this legend (crates/summary/src/cross/native_analyses.rs): `registered` and `disabled` are READ FROM THIS FILE's constants (zzop_facade::NATIVE_ANALYSES_REGISTERED_MEANING / _DISABLED_MEANING, the latter with one clause appended about the join's exclude-only gate) so the two replies cannot disagree about their own denominator, while the other sentences are lane-specific by design. NATIVE_ANALYSES_SHIPPED_OFF_MEANING is exported beside them but deliberately does not travel — the join reply has no `shippedOff` key to explain — and the split makes the join's `disabled` sentence stricter rather than staler, since that list is now only what a config chose. Same sibling-key shape and same reason as `packsLoadedMeaning`, and the same reason this repo pairs every machine field with a meaning: an auditor reading counts alone called the nearest existing channel a pointer rather than a statement. UNCONDITIONAL IN SUBSTANCE, unlike its packsLoaded twin — packsLoaded can legitimately be empty, while every build registers native analyses, so this legend is written on every reply. That is a fact about the FIELD; the `carry-conditional` in the column is a fact about the GUARD, and this note asserted the second from the first until 2026-08-29 (see the sibling row for the same half-finished edit and the rule that now holds it). WHAT THE COLUMN ABOVE DOES AND DOES NOT SAY ABOUT THAT, because this is the row where a defect hid: `analyzeOutputView`'s rows state what happens to a per-tree field in the `analyze_repo` reply, and TEST 3's key-literal scan runs over the WHOLE delivery lane (crates/summary/src includes cross.rs), so a `carry` satisfied by the join projection would read as if the analyze reply forwarded it, and a per-tree field's fate inside THIS reply is stated in prose here and nowhere else. Measured 2026-08-29: `nativeAnalyses` was `carry-conditional` on its own row and absent from every byte of the cross reply, root and `sources[]` alike, with nothing red. The structural half of the repair is `_replyRootKeys` below — every top-level key of each reply is now declared, so a channel the join drops (or lifts to its root, as `configWarnings`/`packsLoadedMeaning`/`nativeAnalyses` are) is a declaration rather than an inference, and crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs holds it against a real reply. The `sources[]` field list above stays PROSE and is the remaining gap: it names the element's keys inline, which neither the key-literal scan nor a top-level keyset can see. That sentence used to say it named EIGHT while the list it points at names ten, three of them optional (2026-09-12, review ledger V168) — so the count is gone and the list is the list. The raw per-tree output is available via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding).

crossLayer.note: cross_repo shapes crossLayer into bucket ROW counts (`buckets.*` — one row per recorded call site), capped edges (`edges`, DEFAULT_EDGES_LIMIT=200, with `edgesTruncated` disclosure), and UNCAPPED DEDUPED bucket keys (`distinctBucketKeys`/`distinctBucketKeyFirstSites` — every distinct key, no truncation field; the 20-key DEFAULT_BUCKET_KEYS_LIMIT and its `bucketKeysTruncated` disclosure were deleted 2026-07-29) — never the raw CrossLayerResult object verbatim. The two views count DIFFERENT things, so `buckets.X >= len(distinctBucketKeys.X)` (measured on cases/: unprovidedConsumes 23 rows / 14 keys, edges 18 / 11), and the reply carries a run-invariant `bucketMeaning` sentence stating exactly that — the arithmetic is answered on the wire, not left to a reader who diffs the two numbers and finds nothing that explains them. Renamed 2026-07-31 from `bucketKeys`/`bucketKeySites` (pre-1.0 breaking rename, same precedent as census `sourceFiles` -> `parserDispatched`): a wire field's NAME must state its membership rule, and the old sites field was plural while carrying only the FIRST site per key. The raw edges/unprovidedConsumes/unconsumedProvides/unresolvedConsumes/externalConsumes/ambiguousConsumes buckets are available via the raw zzop-facade output (direct engine embedding) and, since 2026-07-26, VERBATIM AND UNCAPPED from the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane — plus as UNCAPPED IDENTITY (kind/key/bucket/source, no file or line) from the CLI-only `zzop manifest` lane (both in `_cliOnlyLanes`). The edges cap is why the manifest lane still exists: above it, two runs' replies agree on the edge COUNTS while neither can say which route left the join. Bucket MEMBERSHIP no longer needs that lane.

crossLayerFindings.note: Shaped via output::shape_findings identically to per-tree findings (total/bySeverity/byRule/byRuleMeaning/shown/shownMeaning+truncated?+testPaths?+buildPaths?+note?+ruleMessages?+ruleMessagesMeaning?+ruleMessageTemplates?+ruleMessageTemplatesMeaning?, with the same {shown, totalMatching, severitiesNotShown, hint} truncation object) — never the raw array verbatim. The prose fold applies here identically, one shaper feeding both lanes. Each entry of `shown` carries `message` as a string always; a text that MORE THAN ONE shown finding carries AND whose folding removes more bytes than the pointer, the `messageRef` field and the table cost to add is stored once in a sibling `ruleMessages` object (`{key: text}`, keyed by rule id, `<ruleId>#2` for a rule's later distinct texts) and those findings carry `messageRef` holding the key plus a short pointer `message`. The gate is net bytes, not repetition, and it is applied per text: a short message repeated inside one reply stays inline while a long one beside it folds, because the pointer plus the field plus the row cost about 260 bytes a finding and 45 of the 118 shipped messages are cheaper carried twice than folded once. A SECOND table folds what that key cannot reach: a rule that writes a finding's own subject into its prose (a table name, a symbol, a cycle path) emits a different string every time, so its shared segments are stored in a sibling `ruleMessageTemplates` (`{ruleId: [segment, ...]}`, keyed by the rule id with no `#N`) and each such finding carries `templateParts`, the bytes that differ, in order. Rebuild by interleaving segment-first and ending on the last segment; `templateParts` is always exactly one shorter than the template, a segment may be empty at either end, one template serves a rule, and no finding ever carries both `templateParts` and `messageRef`. Same net-byte gate and same losslessness — measured on the `analyze` lane against cal.com at `--limit 1000`, 1,705,102 to 993,947 bytes (-41.7%) with all 1,000 messages rebuilding byte-identically, and at `--limit 50` byte-identical to the reply before it, because a fifty-row window holds no template worth its pointer. Both `ruleMessages` and its legend `ruleMessagesMeaning` are additive-only — absent, never empty — so a reply whose every message is unique is byte-identical to what it was before the fold existed. The fold runs on `shown` AFTER the cap, is lossless (`crates/summary/src/output/rule_prose/`), and moves no count: resolve with `ruleMessages[finding.messageRef]` or `ruleMessageTemplates[finding.ruleId]`, never by parsing the pointer sentence, which `VERSIONING.md` keeps explicitly outside the compatibility surface while freezing the field names. One deliberate difference: no tree's `buildScriptPaths` is passed here, because a cross-layer finding straddles two trees and picking one tree's manifest would demote the other's paths on a name collision; the tree-independent half of the axis (anything under .github/, plus *.example) still applies.

warnings.note: ALWAYS written to `summary.warnings`, empty array included (`crates/summary/src/cross.rs`) — the same always-present contract the per-tree warnings/configWarnings fields already had. It was presence-gated until 2026-07-31, which made "this run self-reported nothing" and "this build has no run-level warning channel" the same bytes; the `.get()` on the SOURCE field stays defensive about older engine output, and its absence yields `[]` rather than a judgment. History: this row was the registry's first catch — when first authored, no delivery surface read the run-level field at all (the parallel-implementation-tripwire self-report was silently dropped), the exact shape this registry exists to prevent.

disclosure.note: Carried as a FOLD since 2026-07-29 (crates/summary/src/output/disclosure.rs): the reply gets the registry's counts plus a pointer (`zzop contract disclosure-classes` / `zzop://contract/disclosure-classes`), never the ~10.6KB of run-invariant prose. The full text is available from the contract lane on both surfaces and, verbatim, from the CLI-only `zzop facts` lane.

_replyRootKeys._doc: EVERY TOP-LEVEL KEY OF EACH SHIPPED REPLY, declared. This block exists because the field rows above cannot cover the replies: their key sets are pinned to the FACADE VIEWS (surface_parity.rs TEST 1/2 make `analyzeOutputView` equal AnalyzeOutputView's pinned keys and `multiAnalyzeOutputView` equal MultiAnalyzeOutputView's), so a reply key that is not a view field — a projection (`sources`, `architecture`), a legend (`bucketMeaning`), a census (`buckets`, `coverageGaps`), or a per-tree field the join lifts to its root (`configWarnings`, `packsLoadedMeaning`, `nativeAnalyses`) — can hold no row, and therefore no status, and therefore no guard. That is a blind spot in the SUBJECT of the registry, not in its checks: the guards were green while a channel this repo had just built was absent from an entire reply. Measured 2026-08-29 on the nine-repo corpus: `zzop cross` carried no `nativeAnalyses` at the root or on any of nine `sources[]` rows, one day after the sibling reply gained it, and the only thing that would have gone red is a test nobody had written. WHAT `presence` MEANS: `always` = the key is on every reply this build produces and crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs asserts it against a real one; `conditional` = it may legitimately be absent (a cap that did not bite, an older engine, a phase that did not run) and only its unexpected PRESENCE is uncheckable — so the `why` has to name the condition. WHAT THIS BUYS: a new reply key is either declared here or the keyset pin goes red naming it, so `it is on the wire and nothing says so` stops being reachable by accident. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, stated so the next reader does not read more into a green build than is there: keys NESTED inside a reply (the eight fields of a `sources[]` row, the members of `architecture`, the shape of `findings`) are outside it — a top-level keyset cannot see them, and `multiAnalyzeOutputView.trees`'s note is still prose on that point.

analyze_repo._doc: The `analyze_repo` MCP reply == the `zzop analyze` stdout document, shaped by crates/summary/src/analyze/. SUBJECT: the TREE-mode reply, which is what crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs builds and what the `presence` values below are read against. The ENVELOPE lane (`analyze_envelope`) runs the same shaper over an input with no filesystem root, no config file and no git history, so it omits `path`, `config` and `architecture`; that lane is pinned key by key in crates/summary/src/analyze/tests.rs, which reads THIS BLOCK as its whitelist of keys the shaper invents — so a key declared here is declared once and both pins see it. Keys that ARE `analyzeOutputView` fields are governed by their own rows above and are not repeated here. HISTORY: these five lived as a Rust const (`SHAPER_INVENTED_KEYS`) until 2026-08-29, when the join reply needed the same declaration and a second hand list would have been the second owner of one fact; the const now reads this block.

architecture.why: Present only when GIT SIGNALS ran for this tree (`architecture_summary` returns None otherwise) — absent, never null, which is the distinction the always-serialized `gitWindow` beside it exists to make readable. It is the compact summary the reply publishes INSTEAD of the raw `health`/`recommendations`/`critical`/`scores` fields (each `carry-conditional` or `omit` above, with its own row saying so), and it carries its own `painMeaning`/`criticalTopMeaning`/`topRecommendationMeaning` legends as MEMBERS rather than as siblings — which is why those are not top-level keys of their own. Declared `always` when this block was first written, and a real reply said otherwise on the first run: the fixture has no git history. Kept as the block's own worked example that `presence` is a measurement, not an intention.

config.why: The config file this run honoured, echoed back (null when none governed the run). A request echo rather than an engine output, so no view has a field for it. Absent in the envelope lane, which has no config file to echo.

coverageGaps.why: The extension-level blindness census this layer computes, DERIVED from `ir` (which this reply deliberately drops, see that row) crossed with the census's declared-import side — so it is a shaper invention like `architecture` rather than a projection of one field. It ships ALWAYS, empty list included, following `queryCoverage`'s always-present `blindSpots` convention rather than `architecture`'s absent-when-it-did-not-run one: an empty gap list is a measurement, while a missing `architecture` means a phase did not run. See crates/summary/src/analyze/coverage_gaps for that judgment.

path.why: The analyzed root, echoed back. Same class as `config`: a request echo the engine view has no field for, and absent in the envelope lane, which has no filesystem root.

degradedTruncated.why: Written ONLY when the `degraded` path list actually hit DEFAULT_DEGRADED_LIMIT, carrying the standard {shown, totalMatching, hint} disclosure. Its absence is the honest `nothing was dropped` signal — the same conditional-truncation-sibling shape `edgesTruncated` has in the join reply, and the reason neither is an always-present null. The full count is never in this key: `coverage.degraded` carries it as an uncapped scalar.

cross_repo._doc: The `cross_repo` MCP reply == the `zzop cross` stdout document, shaped by crates/summary/src/cross.rs. Keys that ARE `multiAnalyzeOutputView` fields (`crossLayerFindings`, `warnings`, `disclosure`) are governed by their own rows above. DECLARED ABSENCES. This block lists the keys the join lane HAS, which means it structurally cannot record a key it does NOT have -- an absence cannot carry its own explanation, and that is how `nativeAnalyses` went missing from every byte of this reply with nothing red (see the `trees` row above). So the ones worth a reader's question are named here instead. `coverageGaps` (2026-09-12, review ledger V171): present on `analyze_repo`, absent here, and the INPUT it is derived from is present here (`sources[].coverage.declaredImportsByExt`). It is therefore a choice rather than a shortfall, and the reason it is defensible is that the aggregate visibility question has its own surface -- `zzop coverage` and the `check_coverage` tool, which take 1+ trees and whose whole subject is what this build can and cannot see. What is NOT claimed: that a reader of a join reply has been told anything about per-tree blindness. They have not, and the absence of `coverageGaps` here must not be read as "no gaps" -- it is "not asked", and the place to ask is the coverage lane.

sources.why: The compact projection of `trees` — see that row for WHICH per-tree keys a `sources[]` element carries (enumerated there, never counted here: this sentence said `eight` and had been wrong by one since `ruleTimings` landed) and for what the raw per-tree view loses on the way.

cacheMeaning.why: The run-invariant half of `sources[].cache`, at the root ONCE rather than repeated in each of the N rows that carry the numbers — the same split `packsLoadedMeaning` and `nativeAnalysesMeaning` take in this reply, and the reason it is a split at all: the string is 1,045 bytes and a 25-tree join would otherwise spend 26 KB restating it. Written only when some tree used a cache; a run with caching off has no provenance question to answer and gains no key (review ledger V146, which found `hitFiles` absent from every byte of this reply while the single-tree lane had published it since the day that silence was named).

config.why: The config file that defined the join, echoed back; null in paths mode, where no single config governs the run (each root loads its own, disclosed through `configWarnings`).

configWarnings.why: A per-tree `analyzeOutputView` field (its own row above) MERGED to the join root: the loader's own warnings first, then every tree's, in tree order. One config-honesty channel for the run rather than one per `sources[]` row.

buckets.why: Row counts for the six `crossLayer` buckets — the shaped projection its own row above describes.

bucketMeaning.why: The run-invariant legend for `buckets`/`distinctBucketKeys`, saying that a ROW is not the same thing in each bucket. A sibling key for the reason every legend in this reply is one.

distinctBucketKeys.why: The deduped key view of the five non-edge buckets, uncapped. Projection of `crossLayer`.

distinctBucketKeyFirstSites.why: One `file:line` per distinct bucket key — the FIRST recorded site, never every site behind it (`bucketMeaning` says so). Projection of `crossLayer`.

edges.why: The capped per-row edge list (DEFAULT_EDGES_LIMIT=200). Projection of `crossLayer`; the full count rides `buckets.edges`.

edgesTruncated.why: Written ONLY when the edge cap actually bit, carrying {shown, totalMatching, hint}. Its absence is the honest `nothing was dropped` signal, which is why it is not an always-present null.

packsLoadedMeaning.why: A per-tree `analyzeOutputView` field (its own row above) merged to the join root, present exactly when some tree loaded a pack. Merging is order-independent because every value is the same build constant.

nativeAnalyses.why: The native-analysis roster for the JOIN, derived at the root from the per-tree rosters and the join's own exclude-only gate (crates/summary/src/cross/native_analyses.rs). Conditional only in the older-build direction: the keys are `.get()`-gated on a tree publishing a roster, so an engine that predates the field degrades to omission rather than a JSON null. It carries a key no per-tree reply can have, `zeroInCrossLayerFindings`. See analyzeOutputView.nativeAnalyses for the field itself and crates/summary/tests/cross_native_analyses.rs for the behavioural pin.

nativeAnalysesMeaning.why: The legend for the roster above, moving with it for the reason the two keys move together everywhere: numbers without the sentence are the half already judged insufficient. Two of its five sentences are read from zzop_facade's constants so the join and per-tree replies cannot disagree about the build fact; the rest invert by lane.

check_coverage._doc: The `check_coverage` MCP reply == the `zzop coverage` stdout document, shaped by crates/summary/src/coverage.rs over `zzop_facade::query_coverage_json`. WHY THIS BLOCK ARRIVED LATE (2026-09-14, review ledger W2): it did not exist. The registry declared `analyze_repo` and `cross_repo` and nothing else, so every top-level key of the coverage reply was undeclared and a key added to or removed from this surface was invisible to every guard — the exact blind spot `_replyRootKeys`' own _doc describes, one surface over. It was found by adding a key here and noticing that nothing went red. There is no facade-view block for this lane (no `queryCoverageView` row set above), so EVERY key below is declared here rather than by a field row, and crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs reads this block against a real reply in both directions.

trees.why: One row per analyzed tree, each carrying that tree's `extensions` dispatch table, `blindSpots`, `ioChannels`, `joinVisibility`, `census`, `unreadExtensions`, `nativeAnalyses` and `warnings`. The reply's substance; a run with one tree still ships a one-element array rather than a bare object, so a consumer writes one loop.

config.why: The config file this run honoured, echoed back (null in paths mode, where each root loads its own). Same class and same reason as the `analyze_repo` row of this name.

configWarnings.why: The loader's own warnings first, then every tree's engine-side config diagnostics, merged. Always present, empty list included: an empty list is `asked and nothing to say`, and this lane once published `[]` because it had never asked (see coverage.rs's own note).

unmeasured.why: The axes this build never measured on your tree — the deliberate absence of a single coverage score. `query_coverage`'s doc owns why a quotient is refused here.

dispatchMeaning.why: The legend for each `trees[].extensions` cell (structural / lexical-only / degraded, plus `inDepGraph` and `declaredImports`). A sibling key for the reason every legend in this repo's replies is one: the numbers and the sentence that reads them ship together.

blindSpotMeaning.why: The legend for `trees[].blindSpots` — the CAPABILITY axis, derived from compiled-in sightline declarations crossed with the tree's structural extensions.

unreadExtensionMeaning.why: The legend for `trees[].unreadExtensions`, the population `cross` cannot contain by construction: a language with no parser never becomes a structural extension, so the largest blind spot is the one that vanishes from the list.

frameworkRecognizers.why: Which framework recognizers this build carries, so a silent lane can be told apart from an absent one.

frameworkRecognizerMeaning.why: The legend for the roster above, moving with it for the reason every roster and its sentence move together here.

nativeAnalysesMeaning.why: The legend for the per-tree `nativeAnalyses` rosters, at the root ONCE rather than repeated in each of the N tree rows — the same split `cacheMeaning` and `packsLoadedMeaning` take in the join reply, and for the same byte reason.

vocabularyDeclared.why: NEW 2026-09-14 (review ledger W2). One row per tree: which convention-vocabulary keys the config DECLARED, which it left SILENT, and `silentAuth` — the auth subset, called out because its silence makes the reply LOUDER rather than quieter (a guard rule that cannot recognize your guard reports every mutating route as unguarded; measured on one corpus tree: 132 findings with nothing declared, 123 with the auth guard pattern alone, 117 with the full starter vocabulary). Always present, empty array included on a run with no trees: `nothing declared` and `never asked` must not be the same bytes, which is this whole block's subject. Derived host-side from the MAPPED REQUEST crossed with config-surface.json — it needs no engine field, which is why it could land without touching the per-tree wire.

vocabularyDeclaredMeaning.why: The legend for the rows above, including the asymmetry a reader must not get wrong: `silent` is a list of questions nobody asked, never a list of clean answers.

module_map._doc: The `module_map` MCP reply == the `zzop map` stdout document, shaped by crates/summary/src/module_map.rs over the picture lane's own `dep::collect` + fold. WHERE THE SHAPER LIVES, and why it is not under crates/summary/src/graph/: every non-test .rs inside a `_cliOnlyLanes` module tree is declared in this file, and a declaration SUBTRACTS that file from the guard that keeps CLI vocabulary off the MCP wire. This lane is ON that wire, so it sits outside the tree and reads the fold through a prose-free data seam (`graph::module_fold`) — resolution (b) of the three that surface_parity.rs's undeclared-source failure names. There is no facade-view block for this lane, so EVERY key below is declared here rather than by a field row, and crates/summary/tests/reply_keyset_parity.rs reads this block against a real reply in both directions.

fold.why: The grain this map was folded at, echoed back — the argument the caller passed, so a stored reply says which question it answers. Named `fold` rather than `depth` because `zzop graph --domain dep --fold <n>` already performs this exact collapse and one operation gets one word; the first spelling was `--depth`, taken back the same day when it collided with GIT's own `--depth` inside a shared-crate message that contract 16 cannot disambiguate by token. Required on the wire rather than defaulted: an unfolded map is the file graph, which is the thing this lane collapses.

modules.why: One row per module at this fold: `{id, files, inCycle}`, plus `lines` and `linesMeasuredOver` when this run measured any of the module's files. The pair is inseparable and BOTH are absent rather than `0` when nothing was measured — an unmeasured module and an empty one are different facts. Always present, empty array included: an empty map is a measured answer about a tree with no resolved imports, not a missing one.

edges.why: One row per module-to-module edge: `{from, to, fileEdges}`. Edges INSIDE one module are dropped (that is what a module is), so this count and `census.fileImports` are different populations on purpose — `meaning` owns that reading. Always present, empty array included, for the same reason `modules` is.

census.why: What folding cost, computed rather than asserted: `{files, modules, fileImports, moduleEdges, unfoldableModules, fileCycles}`. `unfoldableModules` counts rows that are a single file shallower than `fold` — real rows that could not fold further, never rows that were lost, because NOTHING in this reply is capped.

meaning.why: The reply's own legend, FOLDED: a short note carrying the four readings a map is misread on, plus the pointer to the reply-legends document that holds the full text. It is in the shared fold list (`crates/summary/src/output/legends.rs`), which is why crates/summary/tests/legend_fold.rs sweeps TWO replies since 2026-09-15 rather than one.
